portInfo.description: New York City’s passenger cruise gateways are the Manhattan Cruise Terminal on the Hudson and the Brooklyn Cruise Terminal at Pier 12 in Red Hook, both operated by Ports America under NYCEDC framing. MCT’s main office address is 711 12th Avenue at West 55th Street; NYCEDC publishes maximum ship dimensions (1,000′ length, 150′ width, 36′ draught) and marine reference latitudes/longitudes for Pier 88 and Pier 90, plus notes on full CBP processing areas. Brooklyn’s main office is Pier 12, Building 112, with a GPS-only address at 210 Clinton Wharf; maximum length 1,135.2′, quay length 880′. Passenger door WGS84 pins are not published as entrance surveys — pins stay null. Which borough you use is sailing-specific; going to the wrong terminal can cost the ship.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Midtown / Times Square / Central Park — realistic from MCT with traffic buffer — ~150 min.
Hudson River Greenway — immediate west-side walk from MCT context.
9/11 Memorial — downtown transfer; minutes Not verified.
Brooklyn Bridge / Dumbo — better from BCT than MCT on a short call.
Statue of Liberty / ferry — organised only; security queues.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Confirm Manhattan vs Brooklyn vs Cape Liberty before you book a car — three different facilities serve the wider NY/NJ market.
